teaching.hint: Once the first two pieces are chosen, how much freedom remains in every later partition boundary?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Choosing the first two legal numbers forces every subsequent number, so only the initial split needs enumeration.
solution_outline.approach: Try each pair of initial substrings that has no invalid leading zero. For each pair, repeatedly compute their exact decimal sum and require it to match the next unused input digits until a mismatch or complete consumption.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The two tracked previous values are the last two matched sequence values, and the current input position is immediately after their validated prefix.
solution_outline.correctness: Every possible legal first pair is considered. For a fixed pair, the additive rule determines one required next value; matching it advances exactly one valid sequence step, while a mismatch disproves that pair. Full consumption after at least one such step therefore proves a valid sequence, and any valid sequence is found from its first pair.
solution_outline.complexity: There are O(n^2) initial splits and O(n)-digit validation work per split, for O(n^3) time and O(n) auxiliary space using decimal-string arithmetic.
solution_outline.pitfall: Parsing pieces into fixed-width numeric types can overflow, and accepting a multi-digit leading-zero piece violates the sequence definition.

common_wrong_turns: Trying arbitrary boundaries after the first two numbers
Allowing multi-digit values beginning with zero
Returning true for only two numbers
source_fidelity_notes: Examples were omitted; digit-only input, minimum sequence length, additive definition, leading-zero rule, length bound, and overflow follow-up were retained.
